issues.translation_quote: Senior economist at "Giprorybа", the Fisheries Design Institute.
issues.justification: Translator's gloss is inserted into dialogue; also the name contains a Cyrillic 'а' typo. Acceptable but explanatory addition breaks the spoken line.
The polite Soviet form of address by name and patronymic is flattened; 'full name' loses the courteous register of the radio host.

issues.translation_quote: Fris Street, the fish street, - The "Chikanuk" pharmacy...
issues.justification: The mock-foreign phrase (a deliberately garbled 'rybna ulitsa') and the rehearsed spy password context are rendered flatly; the 'fish street' gloss destroys the in-joke of a pseudo-foreign code phrase.

issues.source_quote: Упал, выругался... Чёрт возьми! Ух, прости, "Чёрт побери!"
issues.translation_quote: Damn it! Oops, sorry, "Devil take it!"
issues.justification: The joke is that the password is 'Чёрт побери' and he must not confuse it with 'Чёрт возьми'; the English renders both as near-identical expressions, and 'Damn it' is not an equivalent variant of the password, so the confusion gag is weakened.
Soviet-style dismissive 'не актуально' is rendered with an odd, unnatural English; also 'the song about the hares' exchange loses the comedy of Gennady steering him away.
Inconsistent greetings; minor wobble in rendering of repeated formulas.
Accent rendering is inconsistent: some instances are normal 'Devil take it' and others are phonetic, so the running gag of the foreigners' mangled password is uneven.

issues.source_quote: [Дальше следует непереводимая игра слов, с использованием местных идиоматических выражений.]
issues.translation_quote: [What follows is untranslatable wordplay using local idiomatic expressions.]
issues.justification: Acceptable literally, but the gibberish pseudo-language lines are only transliterated, so the viewer gets no sense of the invented-language joke.
Carefool is an invented pun not matching the Russian mimicry of a drunk/foreign slip; loosely creative but weakly motivated.

issues.source_quote: Что ж мне теперь делать? ... товар как в сейфе! - А ключ?
issues.translation_quote: the goods are as safe as in a safe!
issues.justification: Repetitive 'safe as in a safe' is clumsy; and the follow-up key joke (cast = safe, key) is not clearly carried.

issues.source_quote: Не положено, инструкция! Не взял попутных - это не таксист! Бандит!
issues.translation_quote: He wouldn't pick up passengers - he's no taxi driver! A bandit!
issues.justification: Gorbunkov's reasoning about 'попутных' (passengers going the same way) is garbled, and 'Stop, let's give them a lift!' makes the logic unclear.
The line responds to 'живец' (live bait) and means he is himself the angler-turned-bait/fisherman figure; plain literal rendering loses the wry self-aware humor.

issues.source_quote: Вы говорите: поскользнулся, упал... закрытый перелом
issues.translation_quote: And you say: I slipped, fell...
issues.justification: The captain is instructing Gorbunkov what to say; the English reads as a question/statement of fact and loses the instructional tone.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: "C'est la vie", as they say over there...
issues.justification: The original deliberately misgenders/garbles the phrase ('такова сё ля ви') as a comic Soviet-speaker touch; lost.
Bureaucratic Soviet register ('общественное дело') is softened; 'Красный уголок' left as 'Red Corner' without any support, hard for the target audience.

Repeated; the housing-office woman's overacted gushing is flattened, and 'ЖЭК' rendered as 'housing office' is acceptable but the lecture gag 'Stambul - city of contrasts' is fine; main loss is the register.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках!
issues.translation_quote: I hope you drop dead! I hope I see you in a coffin, in white slippers!
issues.justification: The deliberately dialectal, uneducated speech (у гробу, у белых тапках) is rendered in standard English, losing the character voice.

issues.translation_quote: the building manager is man's best friend!
issues.justification: The punch of the parody on 'Собака - друг человека' is kept, but 'best friend' alters the idiom; later 'A dog is man's best friend' is reused as a bizarre 'strange phrase' and still works. Mild loss.

issues.translation_quote: Papers? The passport... is ready! The pad?
issues.justification: Criminal slang 'ксива' and 'хаза' is rendered as neutral 'papers' and 'the pad', losing the underworld jargon and the comic mismatch with the boy's role.

issues.source_quote: Следить за сигналом, как только он уснёт, она погасит свет...
issues.translation_quote: Watch for the signal, as soon as he falls asleep, she'll turn off the light...
issues.justification: Acceptable, but earlier 'Это дичь' game bird jokes: 'дичь' as code for the target is rendered 'Game Bird', yet restaurant dish gag mixes target/food; works. Minor loss.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: Only two kinds drink champagne in the morning: aristocrats and degenerates!
issues.justification: Good, but 'Измена' misrendered elsewhere: 'В измене!' translated as 'Treason!', whereas Nadya means marital infidelity ('adultery'). This distorts the whole domestic misunderstanding.
Nadya means marital infidelity; 'treason' misleads, though his reply 'Как ты могла подумать' could suit either. Should be 'Infidelity'/'cheating'.
Soviet slogan tone is reasonably kept but flat.
Fine; minor.
The mock-bureaucratic mix of refined and vulgar is only partially conveyed; 'toilette' reads like a typo.
The Odessa/Ukrainian-flavored 'усё' is approximated with inconsistent apostrophe-based spelling elsewhere ('Ahlways', 'ahll'), which looks arbitrary.
The name-mangling joke (козёл = goat/jerk, 'доить') is not explained or equivalent in English, so the gag is lost.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Who buys a pack of tickets, gets... A water tower!
issues.justification: The rhyme (пачку/водокачку) is lost; 'водокачка' is a water pump house, not a water tower, and the rhyming slogan joke fails.

issues.source_quote: Ну, как говорится, на всякий пожарный случай
issues.justification: Literal rendering of an idiom ('just in case') is unnatural in English.
Refers to the 1961 denomination ('new money'); rendering as 'New rubles' is ok but the joke of the old-timer is minor. Low impact.

issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron's hot, right at the cash register!
issues.justification: Acceptable, though the deliberately mixed proverb is a recurring gag that works only moderately.

issues.translation_quote: Who ordered a taxi to Dubrovka?
issues.justification: Fine; but the interlocking ambiguity 'Тогда ... Ладыженский' passage 'Хорошо, что он не контрабандист' is rendered fine.
Unexplained 'verst' and nickname; hard for English viewers.
Yoda-like syntax is an odd choice to render dialect/accent.
Fine, but 'алкаш' translated as 'you drunk' and 'Миша' as 'Misha' ok. Main issue: 'Как у вас там говорят, топай до хазы' translated 'beat it back to your den' loses the criminal-slang tease.
Added 'do time' clarifies the pun on 'сядем' (sit down/go to prison) but the accent device 'ahll' is arbitrary.
Mildly ambiguous in English; combined with 'Don't worry, you drunk' reads oddly.
Fine; no real issue.
